about.title: Ventura Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Most of Ventura's crashes happen on ordinary surface streets, the same ones people drive to work and the harbor every day. Public records for 2025 list 725 injury collisions inside city limits, with 1,010 people hurt and 9 lives lost. Telephone Road, Telegraph Road, Victoria Avenue and Harbor Boulevard carried the highest counts, and Friday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. showed the largest cluster of reports. If one of those numbers now describes your week, you probably have more questions than answers. LawProactive is not a law firm. We are a free service that pairs injured people in Ventura County with an independent personal injury attorney who handles car accident claims on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery. Reach out when you are ready, and we will make the introduction. From there, the attorney can review the police report, deal with the insurers, and explain how California's two-year deadline and comparative fault rules apply to what happened to you.

items.title: The clock matters in California
items.desc: You generally have two years to file a car accident claim, but if a city, county or state vehicle was involved, the window can shrink to six months. An early connection gives your attorney room to act before any deadline becomes a problem.

items.title: Partial fault does not close the door
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, so even if you shared some blame for a crash on Harbor Boulevard, you can still pursue a claim reduced by your percentage. An attorney can push back when an insurer tries to inflate your share.

items.title: No fee unless you recover
items.desc: Every attorney in our network works on contingency, and our connection service costs nothing. California also places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and lost quality of life, so your claim is not artificially limited before it starts.

items.question: The other driver's insurer keeps calling for a recorded statement. Should I give one?
items.answer: You are not required to give the other side a recorded statement, and it is usually wise to hold off until you have spoken with an attorney. Adjusters are trained to ask questions that can later be used to argue you were partly at fault. Politely decline, take down their contact details, and let your attorney handle the conversation.

items.question: My crash happened at a Friday rush-hour intersection on Telegraph Road. Does timing or location affect my claim?
items.answer: Not directly, but details like time and place shape the evidence available. Busy Ventura corridors often have nearby businesses with cameras and plenty of witnesses, and that footage can be overwritten within days. Photograph the scene, save the CHP or Ventura Police report number, and ask your attorney to send preservation requests quickly.

items.question: What if I was hit by a City of Ventura or Ventura County vehicle?
items.answer: Claims against a government entity in California follow different rules, starting with a claim that generally must be filed within six months of the crash. Missing that step can end the case before it begins. An attorney can confirm whether a public agency is involved and calendar the shorter deadline right away.
